answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks by pricing identity: each agent locks a stake that only pays out after a long horizon of honest work, so a flood of fake identities bleeds capital instead of earning it. Reputation accrues slowly, like grass spreading across a meadow - one account can tend only so much ground - while a sudden cliff of new accounts crowding the same ledge of activity triggers rate limits and peer review. Forging a thousand credible agents then costs a thousand stakes and months of waiting, while one honest agent earns the same reward for free.
